title.en: Youth protests across Europe: the overlapping crises facing Gen Z

hook.en: Young people are facing a future that feels increasingly uncertain. Although every generation experiences turbulence while navigating adolescence, the pressures experienced by Gen Z – those born between 1997 and 2012 – are different and seem more pervasive.

sections.body_en:
From climate change and mental health concerns to academic pressure, housing costs, job and economic insecurity, today’s young people are navigating a complex set of expectations. Understanding their frustrations, including those expressed through protests across Europe, requires looking beyond individual experiences to the social conditions shaping their lives.

Adolescence has long been seen as a period of “storm and stress”. This reflecting a belief that is a universal and inevitable period of emotional turmoil, behavioural conflict and identity crisis. However, this has been increasingly challenged.

Rather than being defined solely by difficulty and disruption, adolescence is increasingly viewed as a period of possibility, opportunity and growth. Yet realising that potential depends heavily on the social environments in which young people grow up.

A growing body of evidence highlights adolescence as a critical developmental period with profound implications for future health and wellbeing. There is also increasing recognition that adolescence extends well beyond the teenage years and well into the twenties.

Young people nowadays grow up under intense and often overlapping pressure, and today this is to a higher extent than generations before.

Evidence from the World Health Organization’s Health Behaviour in School-aged Children study suggests that school-related pressure increased between 2002 and 2022 across many countries.

In 2022, among 15-year-old girls, almost two-thirds reported feeling pressured by schoolwork, compared with less than half of boys. The same research documented declines in perceived family and peer support. In other words, young people appear to be facing increasing demands while some of the social resources that help them cope with those demands are weakening.

Parental expectations and criticism have also intensified in many contexts. Success is increasingly framed as an individual responsibility, while educational pathways have become more competitive. At the same time, social media can amplify processes of social comparison, putting young people’s achievements, appearance and lifestyles under constant public scrutiny. For many, there is little respite from the pressure to perform.

Economic concerns add another level of pressure. Rising living costs, high tertiary education expanses and uncertainty about future employment rank among young people’s greatest worries. Across the EU, 40% are highly concerned by rising prices and the cost of living. In 2026, national surveys show that around 70% of Irish adolescents consider emigration for better life conditions. Over 20% of Dutch secondary school students are concerned whether they will ever be able to afford a home.

sections.heading_en: A warming planet and an uncertain future
sections.body_en:
Today’s young people are growing up amid an increasingly visible climate crisis. They hear repeated warnings about the short- and long-term consequences of climate change. Their generation will be disproportionally affected, and they know it.

For some, this contributes to feelings of anxiety, worry, sadness, anger and helplessness about environmental degradation and the future. Concerns like this about a genuine global threat can be a rational and entirely understandable response.

What can make these concerns particularly difficult is the perception that the decisions affecting young people’s future are often made without their meaningful involvement or consideration of their needs. This cycle of intergenerational injustice needs to be acknowledged and addressed. When people feel they have little influence on issues that will meaningfully shape their lives, this can lead to frustration.

Evidence from many countries suggest that Gen Z are experiencing poorer mental health than previous generations. Although patterns vary across cultures and contexts, large scale studies point to increasing levels of emotional distress and psychological difficulties among young people.

Public discussions often focus on explanations at an individual level: excessive screen time, reduced resilience and difficulties coping with everyday challenges. While these factors may play a role, they do not account for the whole story.

Mental health is shaped by the interaction between individual experiences and wider social, economic and cultural environments in which people live. As such, the current rise in mental health difficulties should not be understood as a solely individual problem. Rather, it reflects a response to broader societal pressures that young people face as they move towards adulthood.

Despite these challenges, it would be wrong to portray Gen Z as a generation defined only by anxiety or pessimism. Protests concerning housing, education, climate policy and economic inequality can express frustration, but they also demonstrate agency and a desire to influence decisions about the future.

A 2025 survey of 6,703 young people across Europe found that 80% of young respondents in Germany considered EU membership a good thing, up from 65% in 2024. In France, the figure rose from 53% to 60%. The study also highlighted the importance young people attach to making the cost of living affordable.

These findings challenge the assumption that today’s young generation is simply disengaged from society. Young people are not passive recipients of social pressures. They organise, question existing arrangements and seek alternatives.

The difficulties facing Gen Z are not entirely new. What makes their experience distinctive is the combination of pressures and the uncertainty surrounding the transition to adulthood. Rather than asking whether today’s young people have it harder than previous generations, we should ask more productive questions: what kind of society are we asking them to navigate? And what can be done to make it healthier, fairer and more hopeful?

summary.vi: Thế hệ Z đang phải đối mặt với một loạt áp lực chưa từng có, từ khủng hoảng khí hậu, chi phí sinh hoạt đắt đỏ đến sự bất ổn về kinh tế và sức khỏe tinh thần. Khác với quan niệm xem tuổi thiếu niên chỉ là giai đoạn khủng hoảng tâm lý cá nhân, những khó khăn này thực chất xuất phát từ các vấn đề xã hội mang tính hệ thống. Dù vậy, thay vì tỏ ra thờ ơ hay bi quan, giới trẻ ngày nay đang thể hiện rõ tính chủ động, khả năng tổ chức và mong muốn kiến tạo một tương lai tốt đẹp hơn thông qua các hoạt động biểu thị chính kiến và sự tham gia xã hội.

keyPoint.en: Gen Z navigates a stormy ocean where multiple crises—economic, environmental, and social—converge at once. Like sailors weathering a relentless gale, their [p:struggles stem from systemic pressures] rather than personal weakness. What is one supportive action you can take today to help alleviate stress for a young person in your community?
keyPoint.vi: Thế hệ Z đang chèo chống giữa một đại dương bão tố, nơi nhiều cuộc khủng hoảng – kinh tế, môi trường và xã hội – cùng lúc đổ dồn vào. Giống như những thủy thủ đương đầu với cơn cuồng phong bất tận, các [p:khó khăn của họ bắt nguồn từ áp lực hệ thống] chứ không phải do sự yếu kém cá nhân. Một hành động hỗ trợ nào bạn có thể thực hiện ngay hôm nay để giúp giảm bớt căng thẳng cho một người trẻ trong cộng đồng của bạn?

en: Reflect on your daily stressors to distinguish between personal habits and broader systemic pressures affecting your wellbeing.
Engage in a community discussion or youth-led initiative focused on climate action, housing, or educational reform.
Reach out to a peer, mentor, or family member to share your anxieties about the future and build mutual support.
vi: Suy ngẫm về những căng thẳng hàng ngày của bạn để phân biệt giữa thói quen cá nhân và áp lực hệ thống rộng lớn hơn ảnh hưởng đến sức khỏe của bạn.
Tham gia vào một cuộc thảo luận cộng đồng hoặc sáng kiến do thanh niên dẫn dắt tập trung vào hành động khí hậu, nhà ở hoặc cải cách giáo dục.
Kết nối với một người bạn, người cố vấn hoặc thành viên gia đình để chia sẻ những lo lắng của bạn về tương lai và xây dựng sự hỗ trợ lẫn nhau.
